visual_action: A split-screen video. The top panel shows Donald Trump speaking at a podium indoors. The bottom panel shows Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders standing side-by-side against a blue background, looking at a tablet. After the initial clip, the video transitions to full-screen shots of Biden and Sanders speaking directly to the camera, alternating between them. At the end, Biden puts his arm around Sanders as they both smile.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is shown speaking in a clip and is the subject of criticism by Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders, who say, 'That's everything you need to know about Donald Trump.'

cast.name: Joe Biden
cast.evidence: Appears throughout the video speaking to the camera, criticizing Donald Trump and presenting his own policy positions.

cast.name: Bernie Sanders
cast.evidence: Appears throughout the video alongside Joe Biden, speaking to the camera to criticize Donald Trump and endorse Biden.

spoken_summary: The video opens with a clip of Donald Trump telling an audience, 'You are all people that have a lot of money... you're rich as hell. We're gonna give you tax cuts.' Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders then speak to the camera, criticizing this statement. They accuse Trump of planning to give tax breaks to billionaires while cutting Social Security and Medicare. Biden says this makes him 'mad as hell,' and Sanders calls the hypocrisy 'outrageous.' They contrast Trump's plan with their own, which involves making wealthy individuals 'pay their fair share.' Sanders endorses Biden, framing the election as a choice between someone who will cut essential programs and someone who will protect them.
audio_music: A serious-toned, instrumental music track plays consistently under all the dialogue.
editing_pacing: The video primarily consists of static talking-head shots, starting with a split-screen and then cutting between speakers. The pacing is deliberate and conversational.
central_claim: Donald Trump's economic plan benefits his wealthy friends with tax cuts while threatening Social Security and Medicare, in contrast to Joe Biden's plan to protect these programs and ensure the wealthy pay their fair share.
intended_effect: To convince viewers that Donald Trump prioritizes the rich over ordinary Americans and to position Joe Biden as the candidate who will protect social safety net programs.
